sentences.text: Arganasuchus is an extinct genus of rauisuchian archosaur.
The genus contains only one known species, Arganasuchus dutuiti.
Its maxilla held at least 12 large, knife-like teeth in deep sockets covered by interdental plates.
This bone has a Y-shape similar to that of Batrachotomus and Fasolasuchus, with an unusually long anterior process forming the stem of the structure.
Preserved front jaw fragments indicate that the animal had at least 14 teeth in its lower jaw.
The pubis bone is considered one of the most unusual and unique skeletal features of the animal.
The size and orientation of the acetabulum on the pubis is a unique defining feature of Arganasuchus.
The femur is large and robust, featuring a prominent fourth trochanter and a smaller knob that may indicate diseased bone.
Jean-Michel Dutuit first reported fossils of Arganasuchus in 1979, initially attributing them to Ticinosuchus.
Remains initially thought to belong to Ticinosuchus were identified as the distinct genus Arganasuchus in 2007 based on unique pubis and maxilla features.
Arganasuchus is considered a carnivore because it possessed large, knife-shaped teeth.
The animal exhibited an alternating tooth replacement scheme common among archosaurs.
Arganasuchus is universally classified as a rauisuchian, a group of large carnivorous Triassic pseudosuchians.
The group Rauisuchia is currently viewed as a paraphyletic grade of archosaurs rather than a natural clade.
Arganasuchus belongs to the family Rauisuchidae.
The animal is classified within the class Reptilia.
Fossils were found in the Timezgadiouine Formation in the Argana Basin of Morocco, dated to the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic.
Arganasuchus lived between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
It is debated how Arganasuchus fits into modern crocodilian ancestry classifications, leaving its precise relationship to other rauisuchians poorly understood.
There is no scientific consensus on the precise phylogenetic affinities of Arganasuchus despite various analytical attempts.
